other.about: NAV (T3, design handoff 6.8): the astrogation service's settings. Candidate courses (Hohmann, Lambert arcs on a departure and flight-time grid, torch flights), hazard rules, difficulty points and bands, drift settings and stock ship templates. Numbers marked rough in the sources are order-of-magnitude rules for play, not mission planning.

jump.rule: a generic jump drive (fictional): one jump of up to 2 parsecs in about a week, fuel of a tenth of the hull per parsec

skim.why: a giant's envelope is mostly molecular hydrogen with deuterium at about 2e-5 of it and helium-3 at about 1.5e-4 of the helium (Galileo probe: Mahaffy et al. 1998, Space Science Reviews 84, 251. doi:10.1023/A:1005091806594)

ice.why: water ice melts to water and electrolyses to hydrogen and oxygen; heavy water gives deuterium at about 1.5e-4 of the hydrogen

port.why: a port sells what an ordinary economy makes; helium-3, tritium and antimatter only where a port lists them as stock

sources.mounts: Compound ships design (CM, 27 Nov 2026) sections 4.1 and 6.3: estimated defaults, unverified. The separation push stands for springs or small rockets at a release; the reach and speed for a docking or berthing capture. The rendezvous flight times are a search grid, not physics.
sources.lambert: Curtis, H. D. 2014, Orbital Mechanics for Engineering Students, 3rd ed., Elsevier, algorithms 3.4 and 5.2. doi:10.1016/C2011-0-69685-1
sources.kepler: Vallado, D. A. 2013, Fundamentals of Astrodynamics and Applications, 4th ed., Microcosm Press, algorithm 8. https://celestrak.org/software/vallado-sw.php
sources.hohmann: Hohmann, W. 1925, Die Erreichbarkeit der Himmelskörper (The Attainability of Heavenly Bodies), NASA TT F-44, 1960. https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19980230631
sources.gcr: Zeitlin, C. et al. 2013, Measurements of energetic particle radiation in transit to Mars on the Mars Science Laboratory, Science 340, 1080. doi:10.1126/science.1235989
sources.dose_limit: ICRP 2007, The 2007 Recommendations of the International Commission on Radiological Protection, ICRP Publication 103 (50 mSv in any one year for workers). doi:10.1016/j.icrp.2007.10.003
sources.spe: rough: a few large solar particle events a year near solar maximum, tens of mSv each behind light shielding; scaled by (r / 1 au)^-2 and luminosity
sources.magnetopause: Chapman, S. and Ferraro, V. C. A. 1931, A new theory of magnetic storms, Terrestrial Magnetism and Atmospheric Electricity 36, 77 (pressure balance of a compressed dipole against the solar wind). doi:10.1029/TE036i002p00077; solar wind pressure at 1 au about 1.6 nPa (Schwenn, R. 2006, Living Reviews in Solar Physics 3, 2. doi:10.12942/lrsp-2006-2)
sources.belts: rough: Jupiter-like radiation belts, tens of mSv an hour behind light shielding inside about 15 radii or the magnetopause, scaled for other bodies by their surface field over Jupiter's (the trapped flux a field holds grows with it: Kennel, C. F. and Petschek, H. E. 1966, Limit on stably trapped particle fluxes, JGR 71, 1. doi:10.1029/JZ071i001p00001); a stop-gap until the magnetic fields design's MF7
sources.giant_prior: Johnson, J. A. et al. 2010, Giant Planet Occurrence in the Stellar Mass-Metallicity Plane, PASP 122, 905 (f = 0.07 (M/Msun)^1.0 10^(1.2 [Fe/H]), giants within about 2.5 au, so a floor for skimmable giants farther out). doi:10.1086/655775
sources.relativity: Baez, J. and others 1996, The Relativistic Rocket, Usenet Physics FAQ (constant proper acceleration, turnover, and the mass ratio exp(2 w c / v_e)). https://math.ucr.edu/home/baez/physics/Relativity/SR/Rocket/rocket.html
sources.ships: stock templates for play: chemical (H2/O2, Isp about 450 s), nuclear thermal (Isp about 900 s), and fictional fusion torches
sources.aerocapture: one ballistic grazing pass through an exponential atmosphere: column rho_p sqrt(2 pi r_p H) and ln(v_in/v_out) = column/(2 beta) (Vinh, N. X., Busemann, A. and Culp, R. D. 1980, Hypersonic and Planetary Entry Flight Mechanics, University of Michigan Press); heat load q_peak sqrt(4 pi r_p H)/v follows from Sutton and Graves
sources.brief_g: rough reading of the eyeballs-in (+Gx) voluntary tolerance curve: Eiband, A. M. 1959, Human tolerance to rapidly applied accelerations: a summary of the literature, NASA Memo 5-19-59E
sources.stall: lift equal to weight at the stall: v = sqrt(2 m g / (rho C_L,max S)) (Anderson, J. D. 2016, Introduction to Flight, 8th ed., McGraw-Hill, section 6.8)
sources.descent: Sutton, K. and Graves, R. A. 1971, A general stagnation-point convective heating equation for arbitrary gas mixtures, NASA TR R-376. https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19720003329
sources.landers: stock templates for play, sized after Soyuz, the Mars Science Laboratory, Huygens (its 3 m stabiliser chute) and Apollo's lunar module
sources.sun_magnitude: Willmer, C. N. A. 2018, The Absolute Magnitude of the Sun in Several Filters, ApJS 236, 47 (V = -26.76). doi:10.3847/1538-4365/aabfdf
sources.phase_law: Russell, H. N. 1916, On the Albedo of the Planets and Their Satellites, ApJ 43, 173 (the Lambert sphere phase law). doi:10.1086/142244
sources.sensors: rough: naked-eye limit about magnitude 6 and one arcminute; 10x50 binoculars about 9.5; a 0.5 m telescope reaches about 18 in a short exposure (Clark, R. N. 1990, Visual Astronomy of the Deep Sky, Cambridge University Press)

eye.name: Eyes at a port
eye.why: a dark-adapted eye: about magnitude 6, one arcminute

binoculars.name: Binoculars (10x50)
binoculars.why: 50 mm aperture: about magnitude 9.5, a few arcseconds

telescope.name: Ship's telescope (0.5 m)
telescope.why: 0.5 m mirror, a short exposure: about magnitude 18, diffraction limit about 0.25 arcseconds
